title: ECG-R1: Protocol-Guided and Modality-Agnostic MLLM for Reliable ECG Interpretation
claim: Grounding training data in expert protocols and decoupling modalities yields reliable, consistent outputs from either input type, unlike unverified prompt-generated corpora.
layout: Single canvas, left-to-right flow, with a right-hand step-by-step protocol panel
description: A single flow diagram on a white background, built from cartoon icons and bold labels. At top left, ECG Feature and Monograph Protocol icons feed through dashed gray arrows into an LLMs robot. That robot produces a Reliable Training Corpus, shown in green. A dashed line from the corpus runs to the central ECG-R1 robot, labeled Structural Interpretation. Above ECG-R1, ECG Image and ECG Signal inputs merge into a single arrow. A blue note reads Potential Single-Modality Input. ECG-R1 splits into Image Interpretation and Signal Interpretation clipboards with green checkmarks. A green double arrow between them is labeled Robust and Consistent. A solid arrow leads to a large rounded panel on the right. The panel lists six numbered diagnostic steps, each with an icon and separated by dashed lines, from Rate & Rhythm to Final Medical Reasoning, followed by Summary & Diagnosis.
caption: Left: Attribute comparison among general/medical MLLMs, previous ECG-specialized MLLMs, and ECG-R1. General/medical MLLMs typically cannot perform signal analysis and lack high-quality ECG interpretation corpora, which often leads to hallucinated, clinically incorrect interpretations at test time. Previous ECG-specialized MLLMs often construct training corpus by purely prompting LLMs from ECG features, thereby introducing medical errors that render the corpus unreliable, and they are neither robust nor cross-modal consistent under modality missing. Right: ECG-R1 follows a monograph-defined protocol to generate structured, clinically aligned interpretations, remaining robust and cross-modal consistent under modality missing.
abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) serves as an indispensable diagnostic tool in clinical practice, yet existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain unreliable for ECG interpretation, often producing plausible but clinically incorrect analyses. To address this, we propose ECG-R1, the first reasoning ECG MLLM designed for reliable ECG interpretation via three innovations. First, we construct the interpretation corpus using \textit{Protocol-Guided Instruction Data Generation}, grounding interpretation in measurable ECG features and monograph-defined quantitative thresholds and diagnostic logic. Second, we present a modality-decoupled architecture with \textit{Interleaved Modality Dropout} to improve robustness and cross-modal consistency when either the ECG signal or ECG image is missing. Third, we present \textit{Reinforcement Learning with ECG Diagnostic Evidence Rewards} to strengthen evidence-grounded ECG interpretation. Additionally, we systematically evaluate the ECG interpretation capabilities of proprietary, open-source, and medical MLLMs, and provide the first quantitative evidence that severe hallucinations are widespread, suggesting that the public should not directly trust these outputs without independent verification. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/PKUDigitalHealth/ECG-R1}{here}.
